links.outcome: Patient trust and distrust in ML-based CDSS after receiving information about the tool versus controls
links.effect: Information pamphlet increased trust vs active control (5% [1%;9%], p=0.0096) and blank control (4% [1%;8%], p=0.015); reduced distrust (-3%, p=0.021; -4%, p=0.022).
links.quote: The intervention increased trust in ML-based clinical decision support systems when compared to the active control (mean difference in trust: 5% [95% CI: 1%;9%], t = −2.60, df = 668.5, p = 0.0096) and the blank control arm (mean difference in trust: 4% [95% CI: 1%;8%], t = −2.43, df = 645.0, p = 0.015).

links.outcome: Trust and distrust after plain information on ML decision support's function and purpose
links.effect: Four-slide pamphlet raised trust 4-5% and lowered distrust 3-4% relative to controls; effect was small and measured immediately after exposure.
links.quote: Similarly, the intervention reduced distrust in ML-based clinical decision support systems when compared to the active control (mean difference in distrust −3% [95% CI: −5%; −1%], t = −2.60, df = 670.4, p = 0.021) and the blank control arm (mean difference in distrust −4% [95% CI: −8%; −1%], t = 2.30, df = 646.53, p = 0.022).
